newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM TO TAKE FULL CONTROL OF AIR UK.
newsitem.headline: KLM TO TAKE FULL CONTROL OF AIR UK.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Monday it would buy the 55 percent of Air UK that it did not already own to give it full control of the British carrier.
KLM would acquire the 55 percent stake in Air UK currently owned by British Air Transport Holdings Ltd, the Dutch airline said. No financial details were given.
"Following this transaction, which is still subject to approval from the European Commission, KLM will own 100 percent of the company," KLM said in a statement.
Air UK would continue to operate as an independent British airline and its board of directors would not change, it said.
KLM and Air UK have cooperated since 1980, with Air UK providing a feeder service to Amsterdam from 14 British cities.
Air UK operates a fleet of 37 regional jets and turboprops.

"Air UK's growing route network -- with domestic flights in Great Britain and international connections to Belgium, Denmark, Netherlands, Germany, France, Italy, Norway and Switzerland -- opens up a broad span of opportunities for further joint initiatives with KLM," KLM said.

"The collaborative effort between KLM and Air UK...has continued to strengthen in recent times. The airlines have recently integrated their sales and marketing activities and other functions such as flight handling and technical maintenance have grown closer through the years."
